title: Fundamental of Scientific Molding - Process Development

headline.value: FUNDAMENTAL OF SCIENTIFIC MOULDING: PROCESS DEVELOPMENT
headline.note: Trainer's draft. Uses MOULDING where content/modules.json uses Molding - flagged for a decision rather than silently changed.

promise.value: Build the essential principles behind structured process development.

items.title: Unstructured start-ups
items.description: the process is set up differently each time, depending on who is on shift.

items.title: No development phases
items.description: filling, packing and cooling are adjusted together without separating their roles.

items.title: Settings recorded, evidence ignored
items.description: values are written down, but actual process outputs are not read.

items.title: No shared meaning of "stable"
items.description: teams do not agree on what repeatable means.

items.title: Data collected but unused
items.description: numbers are gathered without a clear purpose.

items.title: Not ready for advanced learning
items.description: the basics are missing, so advanced development training is hard to absorb.

items.title: More organised start-up
items.description: replace random adjustment with a clear development sequence.

items.title: Clearer process thinking
items.description: connect each process phase to what the plastic experiences.

items.title: Better use of process data
items.description: turn recorded values into usable evidence.

items.title: Readiness for advanced capability
items.description: prepare the team for 4-day Process Development.

rows.before: Adjust settings until parts look acceptable

rows.after: Repeatability has a shared meaning and indicators

items.title: Describe the process phases and what each is meant to achieve
items.description: Name the phases and state the purpose of each.

items.title: Separate process inputs from actual process outputs
items.description: Distinguish what is set from what the process actually does.

items.title: Read basic process data and explain what it suggests
items.description: Turn recorded figures into a statement about the process.

items.title: Explain what repeatability means and recognise its basic indicators
items.description: State the definition and the signs that support it.

items.title: Record process information clearly for the wider team
items.description: Document so another engineer can follow it.
